meta: In shrimp farming, feeding by guesswork leads to leftover feed, dirty water and sick shrimp. Cameras count shrimp, sensors watch the water, and a simple daily log helps too.

muc.title: Feeding by guesswork
muc.text: Feed shrimp by guesswork and you easily overfeed, the water gets dirty, and the shrimp get sick.

muc.title: Cameras count and measure shrimp
muc.text: Some devices use cameras and AI to count shrimp and measure their size, so the amount of feed can be worked out more precisely.

muc.title: Sensors warn about bad water
muc.text: Sensors in the pond measure oxygen and pH day and night, and when the readings get worse, they alert your phone so you can act in time.

muc.title: Ask AI about your log book
muc.text: Without expensive equipment, farmers can still keep daily notes and ask a chatbot to find patterns, but an aquaculture engineer should check the conclusions.

muc.title: Two weeks of notes
muc.text: Write down feed amounts, weather and water readings every day for two weeks, then ask AI to make a table and point out unusual days.
